Cost of Capture Sensitivity Analysis Results Compared to the structured material assembly (SMA) sorbent used in project FE-0032118 (Figure 2), the EcoFilter makes significant improvements on the overall cost of CO capture, showing a nearly $110/tCO 2 2 savings when using the EcoFilter. The major cost reduction was the capital expense, which, was due to the faster kinetics (lower sorbent amount requirement), lower cost structured sorbent, and avoiding the need for a CO recovery step. Compared to the SMA, the EcoFilter has a lower thermal mass, which results in a 2 lower regeneration energy requirement. As a result, there is also a moderate reduction in the variable cost which is largely driven by electricity consumption. Due to its roll-to-roll manufacturing process and inexpensive materials, the EcoFilter costs significantly less than the SMA and is instrumental in reducing the cost of capture from $350/tonne-CO to $241/tonne-CO with possibility for further reduction to 2 2 $165/tonne-CO . 2 TEA Report 6 DE-FE0032254 400 $349 350 $14 300 $100 $240 250 $14 200 $63 $85 150 $43 100 $172 50 $98 0 Monolith EcoFilter Figure 2.
